newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ registered unemployed rose 5.4 pct in June-NZES.
newsitem.headline: NZ registered unemployed rose 5.4 pct in June-NZES.

text.p: The total number on New Zealand's registered unemployed roll rose 5.4 percent to 162,581 in June from 154,245 in May, the New Zealand Employment Service (NZES) said on Thursday.
The rise was 8.25 percent on the June 1996 figure of 150,186.

"An increase in June is not surprising given the register has risen in the month of June every year for the last decade and a half due to seasonal and other factors," Employment minister Peter McCardle said.
"This month the statistics include additional registrations flowing from the introduction of work-testing for some new beneficiary groups from April 1997."
McCardle said while it was estimated around 2,000 new registrations per month could be expected as a result of the work-test policy changes, data on the additions was not available.
The number of people on the register reflects those who have chosen, as one of their methods of looking for work, to enrol with the service and who are available for employment.
However, the Employment Service stresses the statistics do not purport to measure official unemployment or changes in the labour market.
The official measure of unemployment is the Household Labour Force Survey, which showed the jobless rate at 6.4 percent in the March 1997 quarter.
